instruction: Install the Chrome extension from the Desktop folder and make sure it's enabled.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: This variation checks that the extension is not only loaded but also enabled. The getter reads Chrome's Preferences file and checks both the path match and the enabled state (state == 1). This ensures the agent properly enables the extension during installation.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly reads Chrome Preferences file and extracts both extension path and enabled state (state == 1)
Metric logic correctly validates both requirements: extension found AND extension enabled
Complete coverage: instruction requires both installation and enabled state, evaluator checks both
Correct parameter handling: metric function correctly accesses expected dict directly (expected.get('must_be_enabled'), expected.get('extension_path')) without incorrectly accessing expected['rules']
Data flow is semantically correct: getter extracts right state (path + enabled) -> metric compares right aspects (found + enabled) -> expected values match instruction requirements
State accessibility: Chrome Preferences file persists after task completion, no postconfig needed
Edge case handling: getter returns proper structure even when extension not found, metric handles missing extension case correctly
